items.title: Idea principal y detalles
items.body: Lee el pasaje buscando qué quiere lograr el autor: la idea principal. En las preguntas de detalle, verifica cada opción con una frase del texto. Descarta opciones que suenan razonables pero no se dicen en el pasaje, o que exageran (palabras como 'siempre', 'nunca', 'todos').
items.example: Si un pasaje describe ventajas y luego riesgos, la idea principal combina ambas partes; una opción que solo menciona una de ellas es incompleta.

items.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
choices: Urban beekeeping offers real advantages for bees but carries risks that need to be managed.
City bees produce safer honey than rural bees.
Pesticides are the main threat to bees worldwide.
Beekeepers should avoid cities altogether.
items.hint: El pasaje tiene ventajas, un 'Yet' y recomendaciones.
items.explanation: El pasaje presenta ventajas, luego riesgos y recomienda gestionarlos.
whyWrong: Contradice el texto: el aire contamina la miel.
El pasaje no habla de amenazas mundiales.
El pasaje recomienda gestionar, no evitar las ciudades.
items.passage: Urban rooftops have become unlikely refuges for honeybees. In cities, flowering plants are spread across parks, balconies, and street trees, and because they bloom at different times, bees often find food across a longer season than their rural counterparts do. Pesticide use is also lower in cities than on large farms. Yet city hives are not free of risk: air pollution can contaminate honey with trace metals, and crowded hives compete for limited nectar. Researchers therefore recommend that urban beekeepers test their honey regularly and limit the number of hives per neighborhood.

items.stem: According to the passage, why might city bees have a longer foraging season?
choices: Flowering plants bloom at different times across the city.
Cities are warmer throughout the year.
City bees fly greater distances.
Rural areas contain no flowering plants.
items.explanation: El texto dice que las plantas florecen en épocas distintas.
whyWrong: Nada indica que las ciudades sean más cálidas.
No se menciona la distancia de vuelo.
Exagera: solo se compara la duración de la temporada.

items.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
choices: Packing many hives into one neighborhood could leave each hive with less nectar.
Honey testing is unnecessary for city beekeepers.
Rural honey is always free of contamination.
Parks in cities contain no flowering plants.
items.explanation: Hives apiñadas compiten por néctar limitado, por eso se recomienda limitarlas.
whyWrong: El pasaje recomienda hacer pruebas.
'Always' no se sostiene con el texto.
El texto dice que las plantas están en parques.

items.stem: Which of the following does the passage identify as risks of urban hives? Select all that apply.
choices: Contamination of honey with metals
Competition for nectar
High pesticide use
A lack of flowering plants
items.hint: Busca la frase que sigue a 'Yet'.
items.explanation: El texto menciona contaminación por metales y competencia por néctar.
whyWrong: El texto dice que el uso de pesticidas es menor en ciudades.
El texto dice que las plantas están repartidas por la ciudad.

items.stem: The word 'Yet' in the passage signals
choices: a shift from the benefits of urban hives to their risks
a contradiction of the claim that cities have flowers
the author's final conclusion
an example of rural beekeeping
items.hint: Mira qué habla antes y después de 'Yet'.
items.explanation: Antes se listan ventajas; después, riesgos.
whyWrong: El texto no niega que haya flores.
La conclusión llega después, con 'therefore'.
No se da un ejemplo rural.

items.title: Propósito, inferencia y tono
items.body: Para el propósito, pregunta '¿por qué escribió esto el autor?': describir, argumentar, comparar o criticar. Una inferencia es algo que el texto apoya con fuerza, no algo posible. Para el tono, fíjate en verbos como 'caution', 'insist' o 'complicate'.
items.example: 'The authors caution…' indica prudencia, no entusiasmo ni rechazo.

items.stem: The primary purpose of the passage is to
choices: describe a study that qualifies a common assumption about commuting
argue that commuting should be eliminated
compare in detail the costs of rail and car travel
criticize economists for ignoring data
items.hint: Primera frase: la suposición; segunda: el estudio.
items.explanation: Presenta la suposición de que viajar es un costo y un estudio que la matiza.
whyWrong: No se propone eliminar nada.
No se comparan costos en detalle.
No se critica a los economistas.
items.passage: For decades, economists treated commuting as a pure cost: time spent traveling was time lost. A recent study of rail commuters complicates that view. Many participants reported using the journey to read, plan their day, or simply decompress, and those with longer train commutes were no less satisfied with their jobs than those who lived nearby. The authors caution, however, that the finding does not extend to drivers, whose journeys leave little room for such activities, and that the sample was limited to one regional rail line.

items.stem: According to the passage, rail commuters with longer trips were
choices: no less satisfied with their jobs than those who lived nearby
more satisfied with their housing
less productive at work
paid more than shorter-distance commuters
items.explanation: El texto dice que no estaban menos satisfechos con su trabajo.
whyWrong: No se habla de vivienda.
No se habla de productividad.
No se habla de salarios.

items.stem: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the passage?
choices: The study's finding may not hold for people who drive to work.
Driving to work costs more than taking the train.
Rail commuters work fewer hours than drivers.
Economists have always valued commuting time.
items.hint: Busca la frase que empieza con 'The authors caution'.
items.explanation: Los autores advierten que no se extiende a quienes manejan.
whyWrong: No se comparan costos.
No se habla de horas de trabajo.
Contradice la primera frase.

items.stem: Which of the following does the passage present as limitations of the study? Select all that apply.
choices: The sample came from a single regional rail line
The findings may not apply to drivers
Participants reported being dissatisfied
Job satisfaction was not measured
items.hint: Las limitaciones están en la última frase.
items.explanation: El texto limita el estudio a una línea de tren y no a quienes manejan.
whyWrong: No se dice que estuvieran insatisfechos.
Sí se midió la satisfacción laboral.

items.stem: The phrase 'complicates that view' suggests that the study
choices: makes the picture less simple than the earlier assumption
proves the earlier assumption entirely wrong
confirms the earlier assumption
is irrelevant to the earlier assumption
items.explanation: 'Complicar' significa matizar, no refutar del todo.
whyWrong: 'Entirely wrong' exagera.
Contradice 'complicates'.
El estudio sí es relevante.
